references.text: Mica had made the carved image and the ephod that were stolen, and had consecrated his son as priest before the Levite came.
The Danites took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods, and the cast image from Mica's house.
The Levite, who was Mica's priest, willingly went with the Danites when they took the idols.
Mica had hired the Levite as his priest and expected blessing from the Lord.
Laban accused Jacob of stealing his household gods, showing how important such images were to people.
Isaiah mocks idols that must be carried and cannot save themselves, in contrast to Mica's grief over losing his gods.
